commons.title: Toda embroidery and poothkuli shawls, National Crafts Museum, New Delhi.jpg
commons.description: Toda embroidery from the Nilgiri Hills, Tamil Nadu, on display at the National Handicrafts and Handlooms Museum (Crafts Museum), New Delhi. The Toda style is called pugur, meaning flower, and is worked by women in red and black bands on the shawl known as a poothkuli. Buffalo, sun, moon, stars and peacock-feather eyes are recurring motifs.
commons.editorial_reason: Description specifically identifies Toda embroidery and poothkuli shawls, visibly shown as traditional craft objects.

commons.title: Toda green funeral1871.jpg
commons.description: Photograph of a Toda 'green funeral' in the Nilgiri Hills in Tamil Nadu, taken by an unknown photographer from the Madras School of Arts in c. 1871-72. This photograph forms Plate XIV of James Wilkinson Breeks 'An Account of the Primitive Tribes and Monuments of the Nilgiris' (India Museum, London, 1873).
commons.editorial_reason: Although identified as a Toda funeral, the image visibly shows graphic corpses/carcasses, which must fail.
